transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kothari (Redwood SE), Omar Silva (Redwood CSM) / Dr. Maya Patel, Ethan Ruiz, Lena Ortiz, Noah Kim (Pinecrest)

Summary (auto): Quick check-in ahead of renewal to confirm capacity uplift, EU private pilot timeline, and contract amendment options.

00:00 Jordan: Alright hello everyone, thanks for joining. It's Jordan from Redwood, joined by Priya and Omar. Quick roll call?
00:06 Maya: Hi Maya here.
00:08 Ethan: Ethan, hey.
00:10 Lena: Lena from procurement.
00:12 Noah: Noah, ops.
00:15 Jordan: Great. Goal for today is to align on the capacity numbers you asked for, confirm the EU private pilot, and walk through the commercial amendment options so procurement has clarity.
00:30 Maya: Yep and we want to make sure the private deployment meets our compliance needs, SOC2 and data residency for EU patients, that's the blocker.
00:45 Priya: Totally, we scoped Private (VPC) before. For EU pilot we generally do a private control plane + customer managed VPC, integrate with KMS for key wrapping. There will be an onboarding checklist.
01:05 Ethan: Quick Q on throughput: we projected 1.2 million tokens per hour at peak for inference. Is that the committed capacity or burst? We're trying to size dedicated pools.
01:20 Jordan: Good question. We proposed two tiers: reserved capacity for steady-state 800k tokens/hour and burst pool to handle up to 1.5M for short spikes. That matches the uplift you mentioned in the email.
01:40 Maya: And latency SLO? For triage flows we need p95 under 220ms for short prompts. We've seen other vendors land around 180ms but cost is higher.
02:00 Priya: Our benchmarks on similar models in EU edge come in around 200-240ms p95 depending on sequence length and model variant. If you go for quantized model with 8-bit we can drop cost but add some output variance, that's a tradeoff.
02:30 Ethan: Hmm variance is tricky for clinical notes. How much regression would we expect with quantization?
02:45 Priya: Typically minimal if we use our calibrated quant profiles; but we recommend running a prompt set eval before committing. We'll include a quality regression threshold and rollback criteria in the pilot.
03:05 Lena: From procurement side we need two pricing options: (A) 12-month contract with reserved capacity + burst, (B) 6-month pilot then conversion. Also need SOW and invoice cadence.
03:30 Jordan: We'll provide both. Option A has a discount for commitment; option B gives you flexibility while we validate quality.
03:45 Noah: Ops question: can we bring our own KMS and HSM in the VPC? We have a dedicated HSM in EU-West.
04:00 Priya: Yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Private. We'll need network peering details, and the onboarding will include a handshake for certificate exchange. There is a short checklist for firewall rules.
04:20 Maya: Also SSO and RBAC - we need SAML for our IDP and role mapping to limit model access for research vs production.
04:35 Jordan: SAML SSO and granular RBAC are in the Private offering. We'll include the mapping doc.
04:50 Ethan: On the rollout, are canary and A/B supported across model variants? We want to route a small percentage to quantized variant then step up if quality checks pass.
05:10 Priya: Yes, Redwood's rollout supports canary and automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity model. You can set quality gates per prompt set. We'll help configure that.
05:30 Maya: Okay good. For benchmarks, we want to test: latency p95 for three prompt sizes, throughput sustained for 30 minutes, and output regression on 250 clinical prompts.
05:50 Priya: That makes sense. We'll run a benchmark in EU private pilot environment with your traffic shape. Need sample traffic and API keys.
06:05 Jordan: I'll follow up with the test plan and the SOW redline.
06:12 Lena: On invoicing we need net-60 and PO process—can you confirm you accept PO?
06:20 Jordan: We accept POs for enterprise accounts; I'll add the legal/PO steps to the SOW.
06:30 Ethan: Any concerns about data retention? For PHI-like text we need strict retention and audit logs.
06:42 Priya: Private supports configurable retention policies and detailed audit logging. We also support field-level masking during ingestion if you prefer.
06:55 Maya: Great. A couple of smaller questions: does Redwood do model cards for deployed variants? We want to capture training data lineage notes for compliance.
07:10 Priya: We can provide model metadata and verification checks; not lineage to training corpora for open models, but model provenance and performance metrics are included.
07:25 Noah: Network lag: what's the expected extra hop latency for EU private vs hosted?
07:35 Priya: Expect an extra 10-40ms depending on peering. Our EU edge is in eu-west-1 and eu-west-3; if you colocate in eu-west-1 you should be near the lower bound.
07:50 Jordan: Back to commercial: we'll draft two amendments. One is the 12-month reserved + burst (option A) with 15% uplift discount over hosted rates. Option B is 6-month pilot with conversion credits.
08:10 Lena: Do you price burst by tokens or vCPU hours? Our finance team prefers tokens for clarity.
08:20 Jordan: We price burst as token-based units for generation and per-embedding units for embeddings. We'll include both line items.
08:30 Maya: Is there a penalty if we exceed reserved? Just curious about throttling vs overage.
08:40 Jordan: We have burst capacity as an option; if you exceed burst and need sustained more, we negotiate amendment. Throttling is last resort but we put safeguards to prevent it.
08:55 Ethan: Let's talk timeline—if we sign by end of month, when can EU private pilot start?
09:05 Omar: From operations side, typical lead for Private EU pilot is 3-4 weeks from SOW sign, assuming network peering and KMS are ready.
09:20 Maya: That might align with our go-live in mid-September.
09:30 Priya: For the benchmark run we should do it in the non-prod VPC first week of August. We'll need sample prompts and traffic shape.
09:45 Jordan: Action items recap: Jordan will send SOW and pricing; Priya sends bench plan; Noah provides traffic profile; Lena shares procurement timeline.
10:00 Lena: One last procurement note: include a data processing addendum and the EU data residency clause explicitly.
10:12 Jordan: Will do.
10:20 Maya: On security, can you share SOC2 report and ISO attestation?
10:28 Omar: Yes we'll share the latest SOC2 report and our security pack. I will link them in the follow-up.
10:38 Ethan: Competitors—they mentioned Anthropic in an RFP. How do we articulate where Redwood wins on cost/latency?
10:50 Jordan: We emphasize production economics — batching, KV cache, and routing policies that reduce token cost with minimal latency impact. We'll prepare a short one-pager comparing typical p95/cost per token for similar workloads.
11:10 Maya: Good. Anything else on the tech side?
11:20 Priya: We'll also propose quantization profiles but flag the quality gate steps.
11:30 Noah: Ops will validate network rules and schedule a short pre-onboarding call with your infra team.
11:40 Jordan: Great. Recap and next steps in the calendar invite. Thanks everyone.
11:50 Maya: Thanks.
11:52 Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript contains minor mis-transcriptions and timestamps are approximate. Shared artifacts referenced: SOW draft (link placeholder), security pack (link placeholder), benchmark spreadsheet (link placeholder).
